messages:
emily (docs): Heads-up: I found two mismatches in the API ref for POST /v3/embeddings/batch — request examples still use `batch_size` while our runtime expects `max_batch_tokens`, and response examples don't include `input_index` which caused a support ticket. i'll draft fixes.

ajay (sdk): good catch. SDK accepts `batch_size` for backwards compat but we want docs to recommend `max_batch_tokens` going forward. please include a migration snippet showing both.

emily (docs): will do. what wording do we want for the migration note? short and practical.

ajay (sdk): something like: "Migration: `batch_size` remains accepted but `max_batch_tokens` is preferred — it enables token-aware packing for better throughput. Test with representative inputs." keep one-liner.

matt (eng): also add a short note that server may reorder inputs for batching. runtime returns `input_index` in each item so callers can remap. that omission led to a confusion case (support ticket 7892).

clara (support): confirming — ticket 7892: customer saw embeddings mismatch when using positional mapping; they expected response order == request order. adding `input_index` to docs would have helped.

sofia (product): +1 to both migration and reordering callouts. could we add a tiny perf note: switching to `max_batch_tokens` often increases packing efficiency for variable-length inputs. add under "Performance".

emily (docs): ok i'll update curl, python, js, and go snippets and add a quick code sample showing how to remap responses. draft snippets below — can you quick-check format?

emily (docs): curl example:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v3/embeddings/batch" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","inputs":["one","two"],"max_batch_tokens":4096}'
```

emily (docs): python example:
```
# python
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="rwd-embed-1", inputs=["one","two"], max_batch_tokens=4096)
# remap outputs
ordered = sorted(resp.data, key=lambda x: x['input_index'])
embs = [it['embedding'] for it in ordered]
```

emily (docs): js example:
```
// js
const resp = await client.embeddings.create({model: 'rwd-embed-1', inputs: ['one','two'], max_batch_tokens: 4096})
const ordered = resp.data.sort((a,b)=> a.input_index - b.input_index)
const embs = ordered.map(x=> x.embedding)
```

emily (docs): go example (short):
```
// go
resp, _ := client.Embeddings.Create(context.Background(), EmbeddingsParams{Model: "rwd-embed-1", Inputs: []string{"one","two"}, MaxBatchTokens: 4096})
// iterate resp.Data and use InputIndex to reorder
```

ajay (sdk): looks good. tiny nit: in JS prefer explicit param object as you have. for Python, show kwarg name to prevent positional confusion.

matt (eng): i'll validate the exact field name/position for `input_index` in the runtime (should be an int field inside each data item). if any change, i'll post here before you merge.

emily (docs): thanks — i'll add a line in the response example: "\"input_index\": 0" and a short sentence: "Note: server may reorder inputs for batching; use `input_index` to map outputs to original inputs."

clara (support): also add a troubleshooting blurb: "If you relied on response order, update mapping logic or pin small `max_batch_tokens` for strict order."

sofia (product): and add a short perf tip: "For short inputs, increasing `max_batch_tokens` improves packing; for latency-sensitive single inputs, keep lower values."

emily (docs): opening PR 1302 with these changes for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1302 — requesting review from @ajay and @matt.

deploy-bot: Preview deployed for PR 1302: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/batch (auto-preview).

ajay (sdk): reviewing now.

matt (eng): will validate runtime shape and reply within the hour.

emily (docs): great — i'll hold merge until you confirm. thanks all :thumbsup:
